narrative:
The model estimates a 67% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that stood out compared to employees the system expects to stay.

The strongest influence was that you have received other job opportunities while working here. Having external offers is a major signal the model associates with higher turnover risk, pushing the prediction strongly toward you eventually leaving.

The second most important factor worked in the opposite direction: your overall career experience of 1-5 years. Most employees the model predicts will stay also fall into this early-career group, so your limited total experience actually made the system slightly less worried about your departure.

However, the third key factor again increased the likelihood of leaving: you work in the “other” sector. This category shows noticeably higher predicted turnover than the medical or education sectors that dominate the group of employees expected to remain.

Taken together, the combination of external opportunities and your industry outweighed the reassuring effect of your early-career stage. The organization should discuss with you how to strengthen your sense of future growth inside the company, while you may want to reflect on whether those outside offers better match your long-term goals. Addressing these points openly could change the outlook going forward.
